texts: good. 'together' is read collectively, so the lighting stays one joint act of the keepers with no spurious per-lantern claim, and the keepers, the lanterns, sundown and the day/year are all carried. (The only rough edge is on our side — 'day 460 of Year 2' has to occupy the ordinary calendar day and year slots — and no rewrite of yours avoids it.)

bad: 'the lanterns' here is an unmarked definite plural, so the parse records only a lanterns-as-a-group burning and never hands the burning down to the individual lanterns; ask 'did this lantern burn mire-essence?' and nothing answers. Make the distribution explicit: 'Each of the lanterns burned mire-essence.'

mixed: the per-lantern rule and its past tense are right, but the translator unpacked 'salt-bloomed' into a bare 'bloomed' and so asserts of every lantern a property your text never states. Write the bloom as a thing rather than a coined hyphenated adjective and nothing gets unpacked: 'Each of the lanterns of the Middle Row had a salt bloom.'

bad: 'The mire-essence' cannot be linked back to the mire-essence of the earlier sentence — that one was recorded as the bare substance, this one mints a second, unconnected batch — so the passage ends up holding two separate lots of essence and the slow burning attaches to the wrong one. Fold the manner into the burning clause instead: 'Each of the lanterns burned mire-essence slowly.' If you need it as its own sentence, make it a standing fact about the substance — 'Mire-essence burns slowly.' — which does attach to the same symbol.

good. the cold wind, the striking, the salt-bloomed lanterns of the Middle Row and the night are all carried, and the lanterns correctly reuse the group introduced earlier rather than starting a new set.

mixed: the per-lantern rule, the 'stayed' continuation tag and the record of 'each' are all right, but the plain 'this lantern is lit' half of that rule lost its past marking, so it reads as a state still holding now. Anchoring the clause in time points the translator at the worked past-copular pattern: 'Each of the lanterns stayed lit that night.'
good. 'Together' is again read collectively — one joint producing event, no per-lantern rule — and mist-light is recorded as a kind of light.

bad: like the burning, 'the lanterns showed mist-light' stays a group-level event with no per-lantern consequence, so a question about any one lantern finds nothing. Write 'Each of the lanterns showed mist-light at night.'

mixed: the handful of nightmoths, the moth kind and the attracting are all fine, but 'The mist-light' mints a fresh patch of light unconnected to the mist-light the lanterns produced two sentences earlier, so the chain from lanterns to moths breaks. Tie it back in the wording: 'The mist-light from the lanterns attracted a handful of nightmoths.'

bad: two things go wrong — the threads are recorded as something the leaving altered rather than merely deposited, and the moths' leaving stays group-level with no per-moth consequence. Both clear up with 'Each of the nightmoths deposited silken threads on the lanterns.'

bad: 'the keepers … collected' is an unmarked definite plural, so the parse records only a crew-level collecting and says nothing about any individual keeper. Mark the joint action the way your first sentence does: 'The keepers of the Middle Row together collected the silken threads from the lanterns at dawn on day 461 of Year 2.' Use 'Each of the keepers of the Middle Row collected …' instead if they worked separately.
good. Hesper, the threads, the sea-water, the boiling and the full date are all carried, and the threads correctly reuse the ones the nightmoths left.

good. 'by evening' is read as a deadline rather than a fixed time, the cauldron sits on the forming event as its location, and the new essence is a fresh batch that the next sentence picks up correctly.

bad: 'the keepers … drew' is again an unmarked definite plural, so the drawing is recorded only of the crew as a whole. The link back to the essence that formed in the cauldron is correct, so only the plural needs marking: 'The keepers of the Middle Row together drew the stored mire-essence at sundown on day 461 of Year 2.'
